MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE HELD IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  OF THE LA VERNE CITY HALL
  Friday, June 5, 2020

1.  In order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19 Virus, Governor Newsom issued an Executive Order that
  temporarily suspends requirements of the Brown Act. The Council Chambers was closed to the public, La Verne
  City Council Members attended this meeting telephonically, and meeting was live streamed on the City' s website.
2  A special meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Tim Hepburn at 3: 00 pm.
3.  Council Members present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tern Robin Carder
  Council Member Muir Davis
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress

4.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Pro Tem Carder.
  PUBLIC COMMENTS/ ORAL COMMUNICATIONS -  This is the time set
 5.  Public Comment
  aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on items not listed in
  any other place on the agenda. Under the provisions of the Brown Act,
  the legislative body is prohibited from talking or engaging in discussion on
  any item not appearing on the posted agenda. However, your concerns
  may be referred to staff or set for discussion at a later date.
  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this item and waited a few
  minutes for staff to check for any public comments received via email.

  There was none.

  6.  Resolution No. 20- 49 -  City Manager Russi reported on Resolution No. 20-49, Confirming the
  Confirming the Existence of a  Existence of a Local Emergency in Response to Civil Unrest. He stated
  Local Emergency in Response  that on May 31, 2020, that he as the Emergency Services Director as
  to  Civil Unrest  authorized by the La Verne Municipal Code proclaimed the existence of a
  local emergency in response to civil unrest. Government Code provides for
  the continuation of the proclaimed local emergency by an official designated
  by City ordinance. The local emergency must be ratified by City Council
  within seven ( 7) days. Staff requested that the City Council ratify the
  proclamation by approving Resolution No. 20- 49, confirming the existence of a
  local emergency.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this item and waited a few
  minutes for staff to check for public comments received via email.

  There was none.
   City Council Minutes, Special Meeting, Friday, June 5, 2020, Page 2

  It was moved by Carder seconded by Davis, and unanimously carried to
  approve Resolution No. 20- 49, confirming the existence of a local emergency in
  response to civil unrest.

  Resolution  No. 20- 49,  Resolution No. 20- 49 -  A RESOLUTION OF THE LA VERNE CITY
  Confirming the Existence of a  COUNCIL, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA,
  Local Emergency in Response  CONFIRMING THE EXISTENCE OF A LOCAL EMERGENCY IN
  to Civil Unrest  RESPONSE TO CIVIL UNREST. Approved.

  Council Member Davis stated he was fully in support of the resolution, which is
  fiscally prudent and provides additional protection to the community.

  Mayor Hepburn agreed.

7.  Adjournment at 3: 39 pm.

  Respectfully submitted,

  Lupe Gaeta Estrella
  Assistant City Clerk
